The wind that night was a thief, stealing the heat from my bones as I climbed the spiral stairs. The lamp—my great, burning eye—cast its beam across the black water, a finger of light pointing at nothing. I was alone, as I always was, with the salt and the silence.

Then the radio crackled.

It wasn't the usual maritime squawk. It was a voice, clear and close, like a man standing right beside me. “Keeper? You there?”

I keyed the mic. “This is the Point. Go ahead.”

“This is… this is the Point,” the voice said. It sounded confused, like a man reading a script he didn’t understand. “Tomorrow. 3:47 AM. The *Meridian* will strike the western rock. She’ll break apart. Twenty-three souls. You have to warn them.”

My blood went cold. The *Meridian* was a passenger liner, due in port the day after next. “Who is this?” I demanded. “This frequency is for emergencies.”
